I'm old Wang, been working these 10 mu for fifty years. My two sons work in Handan most of the year, so it's mostly me and the old lady, plus the grandson helps during busy seasons when school lets out. Six mouths to feed but only two of us really in the field.

Wheat-maize, same as always. You don't change what works when you're my age. The land here is decent — not the best, not the worst. I split my 10.1 mu about even between the two seasons since it's double-cropping on the same ground.

For **wheat** this autumn into next June: I'll plant around October 8-12, after the maize comes off. Use the Jimai variety my neighbor Old Li has had good luck with — I save some seed but buy fresh every 2-3 years. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, about 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, then work it in with the rotary tiller (I hire the tractor guy from the village, 30 yuan per mu). That gives me roughly 6 kg N as base. Then at jointing in March I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu — that's another 9 kg N. So maybe 15 kg N total per mu, which is what the ag station fellow recommended a few years back and it's been fine. I irrigate three times usually — right after planting if dry, then at jointing, then at grain-filling. Water from my share of the village well, but the electricity for pumping adds up, maybe 25 yuan per mu per irrigation.

For **maize** June to September: plant right after wheat harvest, maybe June 15-18, can't waste a day because the season is tight. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the seed shop has that year — around 40 yuan per mu. No-till planting through the wheat stubble with a hired seeder. Less fertilizer than wheat because the residual helps — maybe 12 kg N per mu, put down as compound at planting and some urea at the big-flare stage. Maize here doesn't need much irrigation if the summer rains come, but I keep the well ready for a drought stretch in July-August.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring, and usually one aphid spray. On maize, one herbicide, maybe one insecticide if I see borers. Nothing fancy.

Expected yield: wheat maybe 450 kg/mu if the year is normal, maize around 500 kg/mu. Last year's wheat was 440, maize was 520, so that's my benchmark.
